introduction.zh: 黑夜里，医生和动物们悄悄起了锚，想把船开出海湾。偏偏这时，小猪咕咕打了一个响得不能再响的喷嚏。湾口被另一条船堵住了，海盗头子隔着水喊话，说要拿鸭子和猪当晚饭。这一船人还能悄悄走掉吗？
introduction.en: In the dark the Doctor and his animals pull up the anchor without a sound. Then Gub-Gub sneezes. The pirates block the harbour mouth, and their chief shouts across the water that he wants duck and pork for supper. Can anyone still slip away?

sentences: 要不是那头小猪在岛上吃潮湿的甘蔗时受了凉，本来一切都会顺顺当当的。
事情是这样发生的：
他们一声不响地起了锚，正把船小心翼翼地从海湾里开出去，咕咕忽然打了个喷嚏，响得另一条船上的海盗都冲上楼来，看看是什么声音。

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生养的小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor’s little pig.

sentences: 他们一看医生要逃走，就把另一条船横着驶到湾口，好让医生出不了外海。
于是这些坏人的头子（他自称「本·阿里，巨龙」）冲医生挥着拳头，隔着水大喊：

hints.zh: 本·阿里，这伙海盗的头子，诨号「巴巴里巨龙」。
hints.en: Ben Ali, the chief of these pirates, who calls himself the Dragon.

sentences: 哈！
你被逮住了，我的好朋友！
你打算坐着我的船溜走，是吧？
可你的航海本事还不够好，斗不过巴巴里巨龙本·阿里。
我要你那只鸭子——还有那头猪。
今儿晚饭我们就吃猪排和烤鸭。
在我放你回家之前，你得让你的朋友们给我送一箱子黄金来。」

hints.zh: 巴巴里巨龙，本·阿里的诨名；巴巴里指北非海岸一带。
hints.en: The Barbary Dragon: Ben Ali’s nickname; Barbary is the old name for the North African coast.

sentences: 可怜的咕咕哭了起来；达布达布准备飞走逃命。
可是猫头鹰图图对医生低声说：

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor’s duck.

hints.zh: 图图，医生的猫头鹰。
hints.en: Too-Too, the Doctor’s owl.

sentences: 「一直跟他说话，医生。
对他客气些。
我们这条旧船很快就要沉了——老鼠们说，明天夜里之前它就会沉到海底——老鼠从没说错过。
对他客气些，一直拖到船在他脚下沉下去。
一直跟他说话。」

hints.zh: be bound to + 动词，意思是「一定会、必定」：这条船非沉不可。
hints.en: Be bound to do something means it is certain to happen: the ship is sure to sink.

quiz.question: Why do the pirates on the other ship come rushing upstairs?
options: Gub-Gub sneezes very loudly.
They hear the anchor being pulled up.
The Doctor calls out to them.

feedback.zh: 原文说咕咕一个喷嚏响得让另一条船上的海盗都冲上楼来看是什么声音，悄悄逃走就这么暴露了。
feedback.en: Gub-Gub’s sneeze was so loud that the pirates on the other ship rushed upstairs to see what the noise was.

quiz.question: Why does Too-Too tell the Doctor to keep talking and be pleasant?
options: Because their old ship is sure to sink soon.
Because the pirates will get tired and sail away.
Because another ship is coming to help them.

feedback.zh: 图图说旧船很快会沉，老鼠讲过明天夜里之前它就到海底，所以要医生拖延时间，等船在海盗脚下沉掉。
feedback.en: Too-Too says the old ship is bound to sink before the next night, so the Doctor should keep the pirate talking until it goes down under him.

grammar.excerpt: As soon as they saw that the Doctor was escaping

focus.zh: as soon as 引出先发生的事：他们一看出医生要逃，主句紧接着讲海盗马上把船横到湾口。
focus.en: As soon as marks the first event: the moment they saw the Doctor escaping, the pirates blocked the bay.

introduction.zh: 医生答应了图图的办法，可这一整夜该跟海盗聊些什么？吉普觉得根本不用聊：对方只有六个人，咬个真海盗，回家才好讲给隔壁的牧羊犬听。医生说他们有手枪和刀。船越来越近，海盗的笑声却忽然停了。
introduction.en: Too-Too’s plan is simple: keep the pirate talking. But what can the Doctor talk about all night? Jip thinks talking is a waste — there are only six pirates, and he would love to bite a real one. Then the pirates come closer, and their laughing stops.

sentences: 「什么，要到明天夜里！」医生说。
「好吧，我尽力而为……
让我想想——我该说些什么呢？」
「噢，让他们来吧，」吉普说。
「我们能收拾这些脏兮兮的坏蛋。
他们只有六个人。
让他们来吧。
等我们回了家，我真想告诉隔壁那条牧羊犬，我咬过一个真正的海盗。
让他们来吧。
我们能打赢他们。」

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor’s dog.

hints.zh: ’em 是 them 的口语缩写，Let ’em come 就是「让他们来吧」，比 Let them come 更随意。
hints.en: ’Em is a spoken short form of them: let ’em come means let them come.

sentences: 「可他们有手枪和刀，」医生说。
「不行，那可不行。
我得跟他谈谈……
你听着，本·阿里——」
可医生还没再说下去，海盗们已经把船驶得更近，兴高采烈地笑着，互相问：「谁第一个去抓那头猪？」
可怜的咕咕吓坏了；「推我拉你」开始在船桅上磨角，准备打一架；吉普则不停地跳起来叫，用狗话骂本·阿里。

hints.zh: 「推我拉你」，那只两个头的奇怪动物；本书固定译名。
hints.en: The pushmi-pullyu, the two-headed animal; the name is written with a hyphen.

sentences: 可过了一会儿，海盗们那边好像出了什么岔子；他们不笑了，也不说笑话了；他们满脸困惑；有什么东西让他们不安起来。

hints.zh: crack jokes 是「说笑话、讲俏皮话」，不是「把笑话弄裂」。
hints.en: To crack jokes means to tell jokes and make fun; nothing is being broken.

sentences: 接着，本·阿里低头盯着自己的脚下，忽然大吼一声：
「雷电在上！——伙计们，船漏水了！」
于是别的海盗也往船边探头看，果然看见船在水里越来越低。
其中一个对本·阿里说：
「可这条旧船要是真在下沉，我们总该看见老鼠往外跑吧。」

quiz.question: Why does the Doctor say no to Jip’s plan of fighting?
options: The pirates have pistols and swords.
There are too many pirates for Jip.
The Doctor wants to save the ship first.

feedback.zh: 吉普说六个海盗不算什么，医生马上提醒：他们有手枪和刀，打起来绝不行，还是得靠嘴谈。
feedback.en: Jip says six men are nothing, but the Doctor points out that they have pistols and swords, so fighting would never do.

quiz.question: What are the pirates doing as they sail nearer?
options: Laughing and asking who will catch the pig first.
Lowering a small boat to row to the island.
Shouting to the Doctor for the trunk of gold.

feedback.zh: 原文写他们兴高采烈地笑着，互相问「谁第一个去抓那头猪」，好像抓猪是件好玩的事。
feedback.en: They come on laughing with glee and asking one another who shall be the first to catch the pig.

grammar.excerpt: Jip kept springing into the air and barking

focus.zh: kept springing 是 keep + 动词 -ing：吉普一次又一次地跳起来叫，表示反复不停。
focus.en: Kept springing is keep + -ing: Jip jumped and barked again and again.

introduction.zh: 旧船紧挨着医生的船，海盗们还在笑：这一回跑不掉了。可笑着笑着，有人觉得脚下的船板不对劲，低头一看——水正从缝里往上冒。他们能撑到岸上吗？
introduction.en: The pirate ship is close beside the Doctor’s, and the pirates are still laughing: this time their prey cannot get away. Then one of them feels something wrong under his feet and looks down — water is coming up between the boards. Can they reach the shore?

sentences: 吉普从另一条船上隔着水大喊：
「你们这些大笨蛋，那儿根本没有老鼠可跑了！
它们两个钟头前就走了！也送你们一句『哈，哈』，『我的好朋友』！」

hints.zh: duffer 是「笨蛋、不中用的家伙」，great 在这里加重嘲弄：你们这些大笨蛋。
hints.en: A duffer is a stupid, useless fellow; great here makes the mockery stronger.

hints.zh: 吉普把本·阿里刚才的「哈！哈！我的好朋友」原话掷回去，反过来嘲笑他们。
hints.en: Jip throws Ben Ali’s own words back at him — “Ha, ha” and “my fine friends” — to mock the pirates.

sentences: 当然，那些人听不懂他的话。
不久，船头开始一点一点往下沉，越沉越快——最后那条船看上去几乎像倒立着；海盗们只好抓住栏杆、桅杆、绳索，抓住任何东西，免得滑下去。
接着，海水轰响着从所有的窗户和门里灌进来。
最后，那条船咕嘟咕嘟发出可怕的声响，一头扎到海底；六个坏人被留在海湾的深水里上下浮沉。

hints.zh: on its head 指倒立、颠倒过来：船头朝下沉，看上去像倒立着。
hints.en: Standing on its head means turned upside down: the sinking ship looked as if it were standing on its nose.

hints.zh: keep from + 动词 -ing 是「避免、使自己不至于」：抓住东西免得滑下去。
hints.en: Keep from doing something means to stop yourself from doing it: they clung on so as not to slide off.

hints.zh: bob about 是「在水里一上一下地浮沉、漂来漂去」。
hints.en: To bob about means to float up and down on the water.

sentences: 他们当中有的朝岛岸游去；另一些游过来，想爬上医生待的这条船。
可吉普一个劲儿地咬他们的鼻子，所以他们不敢往船帮上爬。

hints.zh: snap at 是「猛地咬过去」：谁靠近，吉普就咬谁的鼻子。
hints.en: To snap at something is to bite at it suddenly: Jip bit at any nose that came near.

sentences: 忽然，他们全都惊恐万分地叫起来：
「鲨鱼！
鲨鱼来了！
让我们上船吧，别让它们把我们吃了！
救命，救命！——鲨鱼！
鲨鱼！」
这时医生看得见，整个海湾里都是大鱼飞快游过时露出的脊背。
一条大鲨鱼游到船边，把鼻子探出水面，对医生说：

quiz.question: Why do the men see no rats leaving the sinking boat?
options: The rats left two hours earlier.
The boat never had any rats on it.
The rats are hiding below the deck.

feedback.zh: 海盗以为船沉前总该有老鼠逃出来，吉普却喊：老鼠两个钟头前就走了，所以船上根本没有老鼠可看。
feedback.en: The pirates expect rats to leave a sinking ship, but Jip shouts that the rats left two hours ago, so none are left to see.

quiz.question: Why are the pirates afraid to climb up the side of the Doctor’s ship?
options: Jip keeps biting at their noses.
The side of the ship is too high for them.
The Doctor pushes them back into the water.

feedback.zh: 原文说吉普不停地咬他们的鼻子，所以他们不敢往船帮上爬，只能在水里泡着。
feedback.en: Jip kept snapping at their noses, so they were afraid to climb up the side of the ship.

grammar.excerpt: till the boat looked almost as though it were standing on its head

focus.zh: as though 后面用 were standing，是设想出来的样子：船并没有真的倒立，只是看上去像。
focus.en: As though takes were standing for an imagined picture: the boat was not really standing on its head.

introduction.zh: 一条大鲨鱼从水里探出鼻子，问船上的人是不是那位有名的动物医生。听说海盗在为难他，鲨鱼很愿意替他把这些人吃掉。医生道了谢，却提了另一个请求——那会是什么？
introduction.en: A big shark pokes his nose out of the water and asks whether the man on the ship is the famous animal-doctor. Hearing that the pirates are troubling him, the shark offers to eat them all. The Doctor thanks him — and asks for something else. What does he want?

sentences: 「你就是那位有名的动物医生约翰·杜立德吗？」

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德，就是杜立德医生；鲨鱼是慕名而来找他的。
hints.en: John Dolittle: the Doctor’s full name; the shark has heard of him.

sentences: 「是的，」杜立德医生说。
「那就是我的名字。」
「唔，」鲨鱼说，「我们知道这些海盗是一伙坏蛋——尤其是本·阿里。
要是他们来烦你，我们很乐意替你把他们吃掉——这样你就再也不用为这事操心了。」

hints.zh: a bad lot 是「一伙坏人、不成器的东西」，lot 在这里指一群人。
hints.en: A bad lot means a group of bad people; lot here means a set of people.

sentences: 「谢谢你，」医生说。
「你们真是太周到了。
不过我看，不必把他们吃掉。
在我开口之前，别让其中任何一个上岸——就让他们一直在水里游着，行吗？
还有，请让本·阿里游到这儿来，我要跟他谈谈。」

hints.zh: attentive 本义是「留心的」，这里指「周到、体贴」：医生客气地谢鲨鱼想得周到。
hints.en: Attentive usually means watchful; here it means kind and thoughtful — the Doctor is politely thanking the shark.

sentences: 于是鲨鱼游开了，把本·阿里一路赶到医生这边。
「听着，本·阿里，」约翰·杜立德靠在船边说。
「你一直是个很坏的人；我听说你杀过不少人。
这儿这些好心的鲨鱼刚才提出，要替我把你吃掉——要是海里少了你这样的人，倒真是件好事。
不过，只要你答应照我说的做，我就放你平安离开。」

hints.zh: be rid of 是「摆脱、除掉」：海里要是没了你，倒是件好事。
hints.en: To be rid of someone is to have them gone for good: the seas would be better without you.

sentences: 「我该做什么？」海盗问，一边斜眼往下看那条正在水下嗅他腿的大鲨鱼。
「你不许再杀人，」医生说，「不许再偷东西；不许再弄沉任何一条船；你要彻底不当海盗了。」

hints.target: give up being a pirate altogether
hints.zh: give up 是「放弃、不再做」，altogether 是「彻底地」：从此完全不当海盗。
hints.en: Give up means to stop doing something for good; altogether adds “completely”.

sentences: 「那我该做什么呢？」本·阿里问。
「我靠什么活？」

quiz.question: What does the shark offer to do for the Doctor?
options: Eat the pirates up for him.
Pull his ship out of the bay.
Carry him safely to the island.

feedback.zh: 鲨鱼说他们知道这伙海盗是坏蛋，要是他们来烦医生，很乐意替医生把他们吃掉。
feedback.en: The shark says the pirates are a bad lot and offers to eat them up for the Doctor if they are annoying him.

quiz.question: What does the Doctor ask the shark to do with the pirates?
options: Keep them swimming and let none of them reach the shore.
Frighten them away and never let them come back.
Take Ben Ali to the other side of the bay.

feedback.zh: 医生不要鲨鱼吃人，只要求在他开口之前别让任何一个上岸，让他们一直在水里游；另外把本·阿里赶过来谈话。
feedback.en: He does not want them eaten: the sharks must keep them swimming and let none of them reach the shore until he says so.

grammar.excerpt: If they are annoying you, we will gladly eat them up for you

focus.zh: if 从句用一般现在时 are annoying 讲条件，主句用 will eat 讲结果；英语条件句里 if 后面不用 will。
focus.en: The if-clause uses the present (are annoying) for the condition and will eat for the result; English does not put will after if.

introduction.zh: 海盗头子问：那我该怎么活？医生给他指了一条完全不同的路，还要他当场拿定主意。水里那条大鱼还在等着，时不时碰一碰他的腿。一个靠抢船为生的人，会答应这样的条件吗？
introduction.en: “How shall I live?” asks the pirate chief. The Doctor points him to a very different life, and wants an answer at once. All the while the great fish waits in the water, nosing at his leg. Will a man who has lived by robbing ships agree?

sentences: 「你和你手下所有的人都要到这个岛上去，当种鸟食的农夫，」医生回答。
「你们要种鸟食，卖给养金丝雀的人。」

hints.zh: 鸟食：喂笼鸟的草籽、小米一类，当时城里人养鸟要买，是可以换钱的作物。
hints.en: Bird-seed: the little seeds sold to feed cage birds — a crop a farmer could sell.

hints.zh: 金丝雀，养在笼子里的黄色小鸟，吃鸟食；所以要种给它们吃。
hints.en: Canaries: small yellow cage birds kept as pets; bird-seed is grown to feed them.

sentences: 巴巴里巨龙气得脸色发白，「种鸟食！」他厌恶地哼了一声。
「我就不能当水手吗？」

hints.zh: turn pale with anger 是「气得脸都白了」，pale 指脸色发白，不是「苍白无力」。
hints.en: To turn pale with anger is to go white in the face from rage.

hints.zh: in disgust 是「厌恶地、反感地」：他觉得种鸟食这行当太丢人。
hints.en: In disgust means with strong dislike: the very idea of growing bird-seed revolts him.

sentences: 「不行，」医生说，「你不能。
你当水手已经够久了——还把许多结实的船和好人送进了海底。
从今往后，你这一辈子都得当一个安分的农夫。
鲨鱼还等着呢。
别再浪费他的时间了。
拿定主意吧。」

hints.zh: stout 这里不是「胖的」，而是「结实的、坚固的」：结实的船。
hints.en: Stout here means strong and solid, not fat: well-built ships.

hints.zh: make up one’s mind 是「下定决心、拿定主意」，不是「做脑子」。
hints.en: To make up your mind is to decide; nothing is being built.

sentences: 「雷电在上！」
本·阿里嘟囔着——「鸟食！」
然后他又低头看水里，看见那条大鱼正在嗅他的另一条腿。
「好吧，」他沮丧地说。
「我们就当农夫吧。」
「还要记住，」医生说，「要是你不守承诺——要是你又开始杀人抢东西，我会知道的，因为金丝雀会飞来告诉我。
你尽管放心，我总有办法惩罚你。
因为，虽然我开船不如你，可是只要飞鸟、走兽和鱼都是我的朋友，我就不必怕一个海盗头子——哪怕他自称『巴巴里巨龙』。
好了，去当个好农夫，安安静静过日子吧。」
接着医生转向那条大鲨鱼，摆摆手说：
「好了。
让他们平安游上岸吧。」

quiz.question: What does the Doctor say Ben Ali and his men must become?
options: Bird-seed farmers on the island.
Sailors on the Doctor’s ship.
Fishermen who work for the sharks.

feedback.zh: 医生给他指的路是：带着手下人到岛上种鸟食，靠种庄稼过日子，不再抢船。
feedback.en: The Doctor tells him to take all his men to the island and grow bird-seed for the canaries instead of robbing ships.

quiz.question: Why does the Doctor say he does not have to be afraid of a pirate chief?
options: Because the birds, beasts and fishes are his friends.
Because he can sail a ship better than Ben Ali.
Because the sharks will stay beside him for ever.

feedback.zh: 医生承认自己开船不如对方，可他说只要飞鸟、走兽和鱼都是他的朋友，他就不必怕一个海盗头子。
feedback.en: He admits he cannot sail as well as Ben Ali, but with the birds, beasts and fishes as his friends he need not fear a pirate chief.

grammar.excerpt: though I may not be able to sail a ship as well as you

focus.zh: not … as well as you 是否定同级比较：我开船不如你；as 与 as 之间用原级 well。
focus.en: Not as well as you is a negative comparison — I cannot sail as well as you; the base form well sits between as and as.
